name: Executive order of November 22, 1873 enlarging the Lummi reservation (Treaty of Point Elliott)
promises: Not a treaty. The President enlarged the reserve set apart at the Lummi River by the Treaty of Point Elliott of January 22, 1855, out to low-water mark on the Gulf of Georgia and around Point Francis.
today: An enlargement, not a taking. No court or claims finding about this order was located; the Lummi claim before the Indian Claims Commission (Docket 110) was not read for it.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 868-869

openQuestions: The order fixes a low-water mark boundary; later litigation over Lummi tidelands was not researched here.
Audit 2026-11-08: removed a stale line about treaties.json naming the Duwamish as the present-day tribe; it now names the Lummi Tribe with a note. Royce p. 868 re-read: matches.
